Definition: from G4862 and G2523; to give (or take) a seat in company with:--(make) sit (down) together.
BiblicalUsage: In the courtyard Peter sits down among those who kindled a fire in the midst of the hall — and Ephesians 2:6 seats us in a very different place: God has raised us up together and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus. One sitting is in heaven and the other is by a fire on the night of the denial, and the distance between them is the distance between grace and fear.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God has seated me with Christ in heavenly places, and I hold that no fire in any courtyard can take that seat from me.
